proposals.title: Spam, fake reviews and manipulation
proposals.objective: Understand how recommenders are attacked with fake signals (shilling, review spam, engagement farms) and what defenses platforms deploy.
proposals.recallQ: What is a shilling attack and name two practical defenses a platform can deploy?
proposals.recallA: Injecting fake user profiles/ratings to push or bury items; defenses include anomaly detection on rating patterns, weighting signals by account trust/age, and robust training objectives.
mustCover: what fake signals are and who injects them

proposals.title: Group recommendation
proposals.objective: How to recommend to a group of people at once (family movie night, shared playlists) when members' tastes differ.
proposals.recallQ: Name three ways to aggregate individual preferences into a group recommendation and one weakness of each.
proposals.recallA: Average satisfaction (tyranny of the majority), least misery (one grump rules), maximum pleasure (ignores the rest) — real systems blend them and add fairness across sessions.

proposals.title: GDPR and recommender-system design
proposals.objective: What privacy regulation concretely changes in recommender design: lawful basis, data minimization, the right to erasure, and profiling transparency.
proposals.recallQ: Give two GDPR requirements that affect recommender design and one technical mitigation for each.
proposals.recallA: Right to erasure → unlearning / retraining pipelines; profiling transparency & objection → explanations and a non-personalized fallback; data minimization → on-device or aggregate signals.
mustCover: which GDPR articles bite (erasure, profiling, minimization)

proposals.title: Recommendation in games
proposals.objective: How live-ops games recommend content, offers and difficulty — player modeling, churn prediction, and the ethics of monetization-driven personalization.
proposals.recallQ: What distinguishes in-game recommender systems from movie or product recommenders?
proposals.recallA: The catalog is partly generated by the game itself (levels, offers, matches), signals are high-frequency behavioral telemetry, objectives balance fun/retention/monetization, and personalization can alter difficulty itself.
